title: Natural Focus Observation
opening: Absorption can serve one purpose and pull you away from another. Compare what happened before deciding what to change.

labels.purpose: What were you trying to do?
labels.result: What did each episode serve or displace?
labels.revision: What condition might be worth changing?
labels.step: What is a small next action?

notice.label: Notice
notice.description: Start with one recent episode. Note its setting, your physical and emotional state, how it began, what helped it continue, and how it ended. A rough duration is enough if you remember it.

compare.label: Compare
compare.description: Put a second episode beside it when one is available. Compare what the attention served, what it displaced, and the conditions around the beginning, middle and end.

choose.label: Choose next
choose.description: Choose a condition only after comparing what matters. If one clear interruption already warrants action, you can act now; a week of notes is not a waiting rule.

examples.title: Finishing a design detail
examples.description:
Purpose: Prepare a clear visual for a meeting.
Setting and start: Quiet room; notes open; began after the question and the needed files were ready.
What happened next: Stayed with the layout while the next change was obvious.
Duration: About 22 minutes.
Ending: Stopped when the visual answered the meeting question; the meeting notes were ready.

examples.title: Following a feed
examples.description:
Purpose: A quick check between tasks.
Setting and start: Phone beside the work; opened after a notification; tired and tense.
What happened next: One item led to another, though the original reason for opening it had passed.
Duration: About 35 minutes.
Ending: Stopped when a later appointment arrived; the next task started 12 minutes late.

choices.label: Episode 1 served the stated purpose
choices.description: That conclusion uses the purpose and what happened at the end. The amount of absorption alone did not decide it.

choices.label: Episode 2 served the stated purpose
choices.description: Check this against what the episode was for and what it displaced. Strong absorption by itself does not establish usefulness.

choices.label: Both served different purposes
choices.description: Other purposes may matter too. In this example, the stated quick check had passed, the feed continued, and the next task started 12 minutes late; those details do not show that the feed served another purpose.

choices.label: I need more context
choices.description: Keep the uncertainty. A description can be useful without forcing a verdict.

practice.prediction: Name the activity and what you hoped it would do. Do not label yourself as focused or unfocused.
practice.observation: Episode 1: note the activity, setting, physical and emotional state, how it began, what helped it continue, how it ended, and an approximate duration if known.
practice.comparison: Episode 2: describe a naturally absorbing episode for comparison. If none comes to mind, write what detail you would capture next time; do not interrupt an activity to measure it.
practice.result: Compare the two: what did each serve, and what did it displace? Which conditions differed around the beginning, persistence or ending? Mark what you do not know.
practice.revision: Choose one condition that may be worth changing, or say why no change is warranted yet. Similar episodes suggest a condition to examine; they do not prove a cause.
practice.step: Name one small next action and what you would look for afterward. If a clear interruption already calls for a change, act on it now; otherwise gather a few useful examples over time. If recording gets in the way, shorten the notes to details that change a decision.

feedback.unavailable: Saving is unavailable for this lesson. Your notes remain on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete each note; for a second episode you cannot recall, say what detail you will capture next time.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved notes could not be loaded. Your current notes remain here.
feedback.conflict: These notes changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep these answers.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is still unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.

source.manuscript: Recovered manuscript locator: p. 34 in the cited 82-page edition. The manuscript PDF is not present in the inspected Trillion source tree; exact page contents were not independently checked here.
source.limits: Examples are instructional illustrations, not observed outcomes. Comparing episodes suggests conditions, not causes. Duration is a description, not a measure of value or attention.
